title: Inline authoring playpen — editor for structured assistant responses
content:
TL;DR
Small playpen for an in-app lightweight editor that lets product authors craft, tweak, and preview assistant replies as structured blocks (text + metadata + tool calls). Goal: reduce back-and-forth between product PMs/designers and engineering when shaping assistant behavior; expose cost/latency impact while authoring.

Motivation / problem
- PMs want to author example responses (rich replies with bullets, tables, code snippets) and lock structure (e.g., must include summary, next-steps, and safety note) without editing raw prompts.
- Current flow: write spec in Confluence -> hand to eng -> iterate. Slow and error-prone.
- Need: a lightweight in-app editor that outputs both a human preview and a canonical structured response that the runtime can enforce (schema + tool-calls).

User personas
- Product author (non-dev): shapes messaging and edge-case wording. Wants preview and simple toggles.
- Solutions engineer: needs to test recommended tool calls and button mappings.
- Developer: wants exportable structured schema (JSON) and a quick way to link to route/fallback config.

Core ideas
- Block editor model: sequence of blocks (heading, paragraph, list, table, call-to-action, code, tool-invocation placeholder). Blocks have small settings (max_tokens, required_flag, quality_tier).
- Schema export: the editor saves a compact schema (block types + constraints) + canonical example text for evals. Runtime can validate assistant output against schema and apply fallback route if missing required blocks.
- Cost preview: live estimate of token cost and a latency tier suggestion (fast vs frugal) per block.
- Function/tool-call placeholder: product author drags a "tool" block (e.g., calculations, embed lookup) into the response. SE can map that to an actual function id later.
- Snapshots + diffs: save versions and see how changes affect cost/quality in a historical graph.

User stories (rough)
- As a product author, I can assemble a response template with required sections so the assistant output is predictable.
- As an SE, I can insert a tool placeholder and run a quick local test to see if the assistant calls it in the right place.
- As an engineer, I can export the schema and attach it to a route so the serving runtime enforces the structure or triggers fallback.

Success metrics (initial)
- Time from idea -> validated response template reduced from ~3 days to < 2 hours for pilot teams.
- Reduction in manual QA cycles for new assistant flows by 30%.
- % of templates using tool placeholders that get successfully mapped to functions >= 80% in pilot.

Constraints / known risks
- Overfitting templates: templates must allow enough variability to avoid brittle responses. Need sampling-based evals (we can reuse progressive-eval harness).
- Security: tool placeholders map to actual functions; ensure permission gating and audit trail.
- UX complexity: keep editor minimal—avoid building a full-blown Notion-like editor. Focus on a set of atomic blocks.

Rough UI flow
1) New template -> pick base persona / tone + slots
2) Drag blocks into canvas; each block has small controls: required (on/off), max_tokens, quality_tier (fast/frugal/hi)
3) Preview pane: sample outputs (3 variants) + token cost estimate
4) Export button -> outputs: example_text.md, schema.json, quick-link to route config
5) Save snapshot -> run quick eval (tokenized) against sample prompts

Data & infra implications
- Need a cheap eval runner to generate sample variants for preview (we can call hosted API + use ephemeral credits). Make sure previews are rate-limited and cached per template.
- Schema store: lightweight metadata table in Console backend; link to route ids. Permissions required.

Experiments to run
- A/B pilot with two internal teams (Support responses & Onboarding assistant). Track iteration time and number of QA revisions.
- Measure predictive quality: does schema enforcement reduce missing sections? Run dataset of 200 prompts and compute 'section present' recall.

Open questions / TODOs
- What is the canonical schema format? (Proposal: minimal JSON with block array and constraints. Align with runtime team.)
- How to reconcile sample preview costs vs real production (batching/caching changes unit cost)? Need clear messaging that preview is an estimate.
- Permissions model for tool placeholders (who can map placeholders to live functions?).
- Decide persistence: store example_text and schema in Console DB vs S3.

Next steps (immediate)
- Create an ENG ticket to propose schema: ENG-984 exists but needs a subtask to finalize fields.
- Quick Figma mock of the editor (Tess) — due EOW 2025-02-19.
- Prototype minimal React component that supports 4 block types + preview (Maya + FE intern).
- Run pilot with Support team — ask Ravi to coordinate.

Notes to self
- Keep editor opinionated: fixed palette of ~8 block types at launch.
- Consider adding a "variability" slider per block later to tune sampling breadth.
- For rollout, default templates for common flows (FAQ answer, step-by-step guide, escalation message).

Links / refs
- existing progressive-eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/progressive-eval
- runtime validation thread: slack:#runtime-validation

End of playpen sketch — this is a working brain-dump, will refine after quick design sync.
